**[MAX](https://www.maxdrive.ai/)**, a Lagos-based electric mobility company, has raised its Series B3 round to $29 million after a [new investment from Nithio](https://techbuild.africa/mobility-startup-max-29m-series-b3-funding/), a U.S. climate finance firm.

The investment tops up a $24 million equity and debt round MAX announced in January, which means Nithio and any other new money account for roughly $5 million.

MAX said the funds would go toward vehicle financing, battery swapping and clean transport services in West and Central Africa.

## **How MAX Makes Money**
MAX reports that it has deployed more than $56 million in fleet financing and recovered $44 million in repayments.

Those figures come from the company.

## **A Patchwork of Partners**
Through Spiro, it has scaled to nearly 7,000 electric motorcycles toward a first phase of 10,000.

## **Power Remains the Bottleneck**
Nigeria’s grid delivers about 4,000 megawatts to more than 200 million people.

Electric vehicles make up less than 1 percent of Nigeria’s fleet.

The government also approved tax waivers for nearly 4,000 electric vehicles in the first half of 2026.

### [SA’s CrissCross Lands Circle Ventures Investment to Connect Stablecoins With African Payment Rails](https://techbuild.africa/crisscross-circle-ventures-african-payment-rails/)
Nigerian electric mobility startup MAX has raised its Series B3 round to $29 million with a new investment from US climate fintech Nithio.

The funding will support its expansion into electric vehicle financing, battery swapping and clean mobility services across West and Central Africa.

Its investment in MAX takes that approach further into electric transport, where operators need financing for vehicles and the infrastructure required to keep them running.

In February 2026, **[Nithio extended a $7 million debt facility to Kenyan electric motorcycle company Spiro](https://techbuild.africa/spiro-50m-africas-battery-swapping-network/)**.

#### MAX Targets 250,000 Drivers by 2027
Nithio’s investment extends a $24 million equity and debt round MAX announced in January 2026.

For Nithio, MAX broadens its climate finance portfolio into transport, a sector where the emissions benefits need to align with the economics of commercial operators.

The challenge now is to grow its fleet and swapping network without losing the cost advantages that underpin its business.
